findings.description: The bucket has no ACL/public access block set and is explicitly commented as public, allowing unauthorized read/write access to potentially sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss/overwrite without recovery options, which compounds the impact of the public exposure.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the publicly accessible, unencrypted aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted despite having versioning and logging enabled.
